The core failure mode is Turner Construction's violation of the ADA's interactive process requirement. When an employee discloses a disability and requests an accommodation, the employer must engage in a good-faith dialogue to determine whether a reasonable modification exists that allows the employee to perform essential job functions. In this case, the employer failed to do so, instead relying on undocumented performance criticism and ultimately terminating the employee after the accommodation request. This creates a structural asymmetry where the employee's protected characteristic becomes a proxy variable for perceived performance risk, leading to discriminatory adverse action.
